theme: Which gauge is lying, and by how much
title: Which Gauge Is Lying, and By How Much
strategies: declare-nothing baseline: leave every reading uncorrected (reproduces the checker's own reference, F1=0)

population-outlier greedy: ignore the redundancy graph entirely, flag whichever sensors have the single biggest spike versus the network-wide per-timestep median, and 'fix' them with a flat whole-record mean offset (no drift term) -- a real local event's brief spike frequently outranks a modest persistent fault, and any true drift fault is only ever half-corrected

graph-residual disentangling (strong): predict each sensor from the MEDIAN of its direct redundancy-graph neighbours (robust to one lying neighbour, unlike a mean), score persistence via a trimmed offset+drift linear fit against a zero-residual null (a real event's bump does not survive trimming as a clean line; a true fault does), and peel off the single most confident fault at a time -- subtracting its correction from the working copy before re-deriving neighbour predictions -- so one true fault cannot masquerade as false evidence against its own neighbours
iterative graph decontamination + robust regression variants: alternative trims/thresholds or weighted-neighbour predictors built on the same peel-one-at-a-time, graph-consistency insight
innovation_hook: A biased sensor and a genuine local anomaly look identical at that one sensor; disentangling them requires reading the residual pattern across the redundancy graph -- a fault is inconsistent with its neighbours, a real event is consistent with them.
